projects.title: Eagle Stump Carving Project
projects.subtitle: Day-by-day transformation of a standing tree

artist.name: Dan Burns
artist.bio: Maine chainsaw artist Dan Burns transforms logs and standing stumps into wildlife sculpture. This project follows his creation of a bald eagle overlooking the lake.

days.title: From First Cuts to a Recognizable Eagle
days.summary: Day 1 began with worksite setup and rough blocking, then progressed through the eagle’s body, folded wings, head, beak, and first feather layers. The photos are arranged in working order so the carving can be followed from the first cuts to the end-of-day form.

photos.caption: Scaffolding and tools are positioned around the standing stump.
The first large cuts begin removing excess wood.
Guide cuts establish the major shapes and proportions.
Large blocks are removed to open space around the design.
Dan clears another block as the wildlife form begins to emerge.
The side profile and supporting trunk are refined.
The rough form is visible before the feather work begins.
The eagle body and wing are shaped with the chainsaw.
The first feather layers are cut into the folded wing.
Sawdust flies as the body and perch are narrowed.
The eagle’s head and hooked beak become recognizable.
The head, chest, wing, and tail read clearly as one form.
The folded wing is shaped in three dimensions.
The front body and supporting wood are refined.
The eagle form is established and ready for later detail work.
